citations.narrative:
Three voles were not handled as carefully as possible by research facility staff as specified below.
Two female prairie vole pups died following ovariectomy surgery. The cause of death was skull injury caused by incorrect
use of ear bars during the surgery. The use of this equipment was not standard practice for this type of surgery and had
not been described in the approved protocol.
A female adult prairie vole was given a lethal dose of anesthetic for euthanasia, then placed in a container to wait for the
drug to take effect. The animal escaped while the researcher was distracted by another laboratory member. A search was
carried out, and the carcass was found seven days later.
The voles were not handled as carefully as possible by facility staff resulting in the death of two animals after surgery and
a separate incident in which a vole was injected with a lethal dose of anesthetic for euthanasia but escaped prior to death.
Since the euthanasia could not be confirmed, the vole could have been injured or experienced discomfort before it died.
The handling of all animals should be done as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause
trauma, physical harm, behavioral stress, or unnecessary discomfort. Both incidents were identified by the research
facility, and appropriate corrective measures were implemented prior to this inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the attending veterinarian and the IACUC director.
